correctness.rationale: Separating j even and odd gives two Parseval coefficient sums on the unit Zak torus: their windows have squared moduli |ZB_n(x,nu)|² and |ZB_n(x,nu+1/2)|², with lattice shifts contributing only unimodular factors. Hence the exact optimal bounds are the min and max of their sum; continuity removes an essential-extremum ambiguity. This gives A_2=1 and B_2^up=2 with the prescribed normalization. The Fourier aliases of a cardinal spline at reduced frequency t have magnitude s(t)^n times (|t|/|t+ell|)^n. For |t|<=3/8 the nonleading ratios are at most 3/5 and have uniformly bounded square sum, so the error amplitude relative to the unique leading alias is O((3/5)^n), also after taking squared moduli. On [1/8,3/8] the two nearest distances are nu and 1/2−nu. On the outer intervals one distance is at most 1/8, all its subleading ratios are at most 1/7, and s(1/8)>s(1/4). For L=log(s) on the central interval, L' is bounded away from zero and L'' bounded, so (s^(2n))''>0 for large n. Symmetric convexity gives the leading minimum 2s(1/4)^(2n) uniformly in x; any frequency staying a fixed positive distance away has an exponentially larger leading term. For the maximum, partition of unity gives |ZB_n|<=1 and equality at zero; the other component at any chosen frequency pair with distance at least 1/4 has amplitude bounded by a constant times s(1/4)^n, using the bounded square sum of alias ratios even at a tie. These estimates prove all prefactors and frequency localization claims. Hasannasab–Lemvig Theorem 7.1 supplies the frame property at every n>=2, not only large n.
residual_risks: No claim of an exact finite-order minimizing frequency or time. The condition number is the frame-bound ratio, not the square root associated with the analysis map.

evidence: Hasannasab–Lemvig Theorem 7.1 proves frame iff a<n for integer oversampling ab=1/q with q>=2 and 0<b<=1. This directly covers the same lattice for every n>=2, but gives positivity, not the n-dependent sharp minimum and maximum.

The frame region N/2<=a<N, b<1/a in arXiv:1503.02160 reaches only N=2 at a=1. The Gaussian approximation in arXiv:1708.04803 scales the windows with order, so the fixed-lattice unscaled width grows differently. Kloos–Stöckler's bound asymptotic is for exponential splines of order two approaching density one; Stangl–Frederick Theorem 3 is also fixed order two and b>=3/2.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The nearest stronger frame-set theorem covers exactly what is qualitative in this record. It does not supply a quantitative coalescing two-fiber analysis as the unscaled order increases; the other sources vary a different parameter or use dilated windows.

evidence: Positivity imposes no exponential rate. Even the exact classical symbol does not distinguish local and global minimizers without uniform alias estimates and the central convexity argument. Order scaling and approaching critical density at fixed order are different asymptotic procedures.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The surviving claim is the rate and prefactor 2 for the lower bound (and corresponding condition ratio prefactor 1/2), the upper-bound control in a fixed normalization, and minimizing-frequency localization, not any inference of novelty for the frame property itself.

checked_sources: Hasannasab–Lemvig Theorem 7.1 as the qualitative same-lattice comparator
value.rationale: The lattice is a canonical redundancy-two oversampling where existence alone can conceal growing ill-conditioning. The exact exponential rate and factor distinguish stability of increasingly broad standard cardinal windows from mere positivity or an unspecified asymptotic rate, and the limiting bad-frequency location identifies where conditioning is lost. This answers the motivated fixed-lattice question without conflating it with variance-normalized Gaussian approximations.
residual_risks: The bounds do not resolve optimal lattice design or other oversampling ratios.
